contentHtml:
To start a business in the UAE, you need to choose a location, such as the mainland or a free zone, set up your trade name, and acquire a trade license. In 2026, the cost of setting up a business on the mainland will usually go over 35,000 dirhams. Setting up a business in a Free Zone costs around 5,500 Dirhams. The entire process of registration takes approximately three to fourteen working days.

It can be challenging to follow these regulations for starting a tech company or any import business. If you get the right path, you can get into one of the world’s most lucrative markets. This post discusses how to start a business in UAE and the particular phases to get your business organized and operating smoothly.

A Quick Look at UAE Business Setup 2026

Getting a UAE business setup grants your company a huge advantage in global markets. Below is a clear outline of the primary needs, costs, and structure choices for your business.

States and Territories: Business setups on the Mainland are ideal for direct trade within the country. However, free zones are suitable for affordable startups with greater tax breaks and limited access.

Standards for Ownership: In most business sectors, private investors maintain full foreign ownership.

Duration: It usually takes between 3 and 14 business days to complete the registration process.

Which Visa & Residency Option Fits for Business Owners

The UAE investor visa business setup offers you a longer residence. For standard two-year choices, you need a Mainland share value of seventy-two thousand dirhams. The number of staff visas depends on your office space. If your company’s capital reaches two million dirhams, you may reside in the UAE for ten years with a Golden Visa.

Comparing the Famous UAE Free Zones

To determine the best Free Zone in the UAE in 2026, you need to ensure that your business fits with the regional specialty. You can choose a high-end DMCC zone for products, a middle-range zone like IFZA for consulting services, or Meydan for online retail. You may select a low-cost zone like RAKEZ for production or SHAMS for creative media businesses.

Determine the Business Setup Expense in 2026

The UAE business setup cost relies on the jurisdiction you select. A reasonable starting cost for initial setup would be between 12,000 dirhams and 35,000 dirhams.

Cost of a Free Zone License

Your free zone license costs will be quite different, depending on the emirate you choose. Entry fees for locations like Ajman start at about 4,888 Dirhams. The fees for high-end hubs in Dubai can go over 20,000 dirhams.

Cost to Set up Offshore

Starting at about 9,000 dirhams for basic asset security and global holding frameworks, an offshore entity is an affordable option. It has reduced startup fees; this format is perfect for managing your foreign company investments.

Cost of a Mainland License

Mainland license costs are usually between 12,000 dirhams and 25,000 dirhams. However, it depends on the type of business operations. In addition to this preliminary regulatory payment, you will need an actual office rental to get your business card.

Unknown or Ongoing Fees

You should be ready for ongoing costs like renewing your license every year and paying the required municipal Ejari registration fees. It depends on the emirate, but residency visas are priced between 3,000 dirhams and 7,000 dirhams per person. It includes health screenings and ID cards.

UAE Business Setup Simple Steps:

1. Decide on Business Operations

The initial step is to select your main business activity from the official UAE business activity list, which has thousands of options.

Verify Permitted Business Activity

To determine what activities are allowed, you can head over to the DET online platforms for Mainland setups or the specific Free Zone authority websites.

Permitted Operations Require Additional Approvals

Before a license is granted in some specific fields, it needs to be approved by a third party. For example, financial services need permission from the central bank, and health care organizations need permission from the Dubai Health Authority.

2. Which One Fits Better for Your Business: Mainland vs Free Zone vs Offshore

Mainland Territory: Complete Market Access Across the UAE

The mainland firm can trade in the local market with freedom. These firms also bid on government projects in all seven Emirates without a local partner holding a significant stake. 

Offshore Territory: Worldwide Holding

A foreign business is ideal if your main goal is to protect your assets, handle overseas finances, or secure your intellectual property around the world. This particular corporate legal framework doesn’t allow for a tangible operational premise. It does not grant residency visas and strictly restricts your company from conducting business with any mainland UAE entities.

Free Zone Territory: Limitations on Direct Access Across UAE Markets

Free zones vs. the mainland UAE are ideal areas for foreign businesses, as they offer extremely affordable setup deals and full company control. There is no corporate tax on certain types of income in these designated areas. However, these firms could only trade within the Free Zone or on the global market. These companies are unable to get into any other UAE market.

Territory Ownership & Control Market Access Typical Price Visa Allocation
Mainland UAE Full foreign ownership Full domestic and international trade 15,000 to 40,000 AED Unlimited visas depend on office size
Free Zone Full foreign ownership Inside the Free Zone and worldwide markets 10,000 to 25,000 AED A fixed quota depends on the visa package.
Offshore Full foreign ownership Restricted, only global asset holding 7,000 to 15,000 AED No visa eligibility

3. Get the Trade Name

Your preferred UAE trade name registration should directly relate to the legal activities you are allowed to do and end with the suffix of your legal structure, such as LLC.

To ensure that the DET approves it, the title must not contain any religious terms or government names to avoid any possible compliance delays.

4. Get Preliminary Approval

Getting your UAE initial approval for business setup is evidence that the government approves your business startup. You need to show your passport copies, your entry visa stamp, and your trade name approval to get this document. It is just the first approval you need to move forward. It’s not yet a full license to operate.

5. Prepare Legal Paperwork

MOA sets clear rules for corporate ownership and profit-sharing policies. It is a crucial step before final licensing.

What an LLC’s MOA Requires

All limited liability companies in the UAE must write an MOA. This official legal document needs to be written in Arabic, notarized in public, and explained. Your business is set up.

When You Still Need an LSA

Due to recent changes to the law, most businesses no longer need a local service provider. However, for business licenses, single proprietorships, and civil companies, you still need an agent.

6. Office Premises & Ejari Registration

For your mainland business, you need to find an actual location. To prove your corporate address, you need a UAE office lease Ejari registration. Instead, Free Zones offer cost-effective flexi-desk options to keep startup costs to a minimum. It costs about 220 AED to register your rental contract on the Ejari platform. It officially starts your trading operations.

7. Receiving a Trade License

Securing a physical location is mandatory for your mainland company to complete the UAE trade license process. It mandates an office lease and Ejari registration to validate your official address. Free Zones offer economical flexi-desks to reduce startup overheads.

New Businesses Must Know: UAE Corporate Tax and VAT 2026

Relief for UAE Small Businesses

You can choose this safety net relief scheme if your gross yearly earnings remain at or below three million dirhams. Your new business will not have to pay any corporate tax.

Corporate Tax on UAE businesses

The UAE corporate tax for new businesses applies a flat 9% rate only to your company’s net gains of more than 370,000 dirhams. All profits each year below this amount are zero.

Limits and Obligations for VAT Registration

If your taxable sales exceed a certain amount in a year, you must register for VAT. You need to keep accurate records of your sales, provide correct invoices, and file regular returns.

Conditions and Limits to Enter a Free Zone

To keep the 0% preferred rate, your Free Zone company needs to have enough local substance. Your firm needs to make enough qualifying income. Also, it must adhere to all the rigid requirements for foreign arm’s-length transfer pricing.

FAQs

What is the cost of starting a business in the UAE?

Typically, from 5,500 dirhams, you may start a business in a free zone. Almost 15,000 dirhams to 25,000 dirhams get you a business license on the mainland.

Do I need a local sponsor to start a UAE business?

Without a regional sponsor, most business activities are no longer possible. However, foreigners may own their companies entirely.

What is the distinction between setting up a business on the mainland and in a free zone?

Firms on the Mainland can operate anywhere in the UAE. Free Zone companies can only operate in their zone and on global markets.

Should a new company in the UAE pay corporate tax?

A corporate tax is imposed on companies with less than 3,000,000 dirhams in sales. Firms can choose the Small Business Relief to pay no tax in 2026.

What is the timeframe to get a UAE trade license?

Typical Mainland or Free Zone business setup applications take three to seven days. However, quick digital licenses can be issued in less than an hour.

Should a foreigner in the UAE own the entire business?

In both the mainland and all free zones in the UAE, foreigners are guaranteed full control of their businesses.

Which Free Zone is the best value for a small business?

Sharjah Free Zones start at 5,499 Dirhams for a zero-visa plan. Ajman Free Zones are the most affordable at 4,888 Dirhams.

Do I require a workplace to start a UAE business?

You are not required to have a physical space. Several Free Zones provide shared desks or virtual workplace packages for new businesses.
